subject: journey/odyssey
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE landscape 3:2 page for the Odyssey journey sketchbook. Loose visible graphite underdrawing, quick fine sepia ink, open parallel hatching, sparse uneven watercolour washes in muted ochre, grey-green and faded blue, small rust-red accents. Irregular unfinished edges fade into bare warm cream paper. A working sketch with selective detail, not glossy fantasy concept art, a photoreal image or an oil painting. One coherent scene, not a collage, no decorative inset repeated on every page. No writing, lettering, captions, labels, signature, watermark, border or book binding. Mythic scene as narrated by Homer, material details loosely late Bronze Age Aegean: simple wool and linen, stone/plaster/timber, bronze tools, low single-banked oared ships and one square sail when specified. No medieval castle, trireme, Viking dragon prow, Roman armour, classical marble temple, modern vessel or modern object. Prioritise readable spatial relationships and natural hands, bodies, animals and rigging.
Scene: Very low intimate portrait of an old lean Mediterranean hunting dog lying on straw-mixed stable refuse beside a rough courtyard gate, greying muzzle and tired alert eyes, ears lowered and tail subtly lifted. Two distant men's sandalled feet and walking staff at doorway, bodies cropped, no hero face. Neither pristine pet bed nor graphic neglect, no collar tag, no mournful cartoon expression.
Narrative context (not text to write in image): Disguised as a beggar, Odysseus reaches his house with Eumaeus. His old dog Argos recognises him, lowers his ears and wags his tail, but can no longer rise; Odysseus turns aside to hide a tear. (Book 17)
Do not insert a foreground Odysseus portrait. Only include people explicitly specified in the scene.
